name: read_requirements
result:
{
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "REQ-001",
      "title": "Add task",
      "text": "The system shall let the user add a task by entering a text description which, after leading and trailing spaces are trimmed, is 1 to 200 characters long, and optionally a due date.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "Entering text and confirming adds a new task to the list",
        "The new task is shown as not done",
        "An empty description is not added",
        "A description consisting only of spaces is not added",
        "Leading and trailing spaces are removed from the stored text",
        "A description of 200 characters after trimming is accepted",
        "A description of 201 characters after trimming is rejected",
        "A task can be added without a due date",
        "A task can be added with a due date, and it is shown with that due date"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-002",
      "title": "Mark task done or not done",
      "text": "The system shall let the user mark a task as done and mark a done task as not done again.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "Ticking a task changes it to the done state",
        "Unticking a done task changes it back to the not-done state",
        "The done state is visibly distinguishable from the not-done state"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-003",
      "title": "Persist tasks on server",
      "text": "The system shall store tasks and their done state on a server so they are available when the user returns, including after the browser's local data is reset.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "After adding tasks and ticking some, closing and reopening the app shows the same tasks with the same done states",
        "After clearing the browser's local storage and cookies, reopening the app shows the same tasks"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-004",
      "title": "Run in browser",
      "text": "The system shall be usable in a web browser.",
      "type": "non-functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "All features are usable in a web browser without installing additional software"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-005",
      "title": "Edit task",
      "text": "The system shall let the user edit the text and the optional due date of an existing task, applying the same trimming and length rules as when adding a task.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "After editing and confirming, the task shows the new text and keeps its done state",
        "The edited text is kept after reopening the app",
        "An empty, whitespace-only, or over 200 character (after trimming) edit is rejected and the old text is kept",
        "Leading and trailing spaces in the edited text are removed",
        "When editing, a due date can be set on a task without one, changed on a task with one, or cleared",
        "After editing the due date, the task shows the new due date, or none if cleared"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-006",
      "title": "Delete task",
      "text": "The system shall let the user delete a task.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "After deleting, the task no longer appears in the list",
        "The task is still gone after reopening the app"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-007",
      "title": "Done tasks display and order",
      "text": "The system shall keep done tasks in the list, show their text struck through, list open tasks before done tasks, and order tasks within each group oldest first by creation time.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "A done task remains visible in the list with struck-through text",
        "Every open task appears above every done task",
        "Within the open tasks, the earliest created task is first",
        "Within the done tasks, the earliest created task is first",
        "Unticking a done task shows it without strike-through among the open tasks, at its creation-time position"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-008",
      "title": "Single user without login",
      "text": "The system shall serve a single user and shall not require login.",
      "type": "non-functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "The app opens directly to the task list without any login step"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-009",
      "title": "Task due date",
      "text": "The system shall let a task have an optional calendar due date (date only, no time), which the user can set when adding a task and set, change or clear when editing it, and shall store it on the server.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "A task without a due date is valid and can be saved",
        "A due date entered when adding a task is saved with the task",
        "A due date can be set, changed and cleared when editing a task",
        "An invalid date is rejected and the previously stored due date is kept (or none when adding, no task is created)",
        "The due date contains no time component",
        "The due date is still present after reopening the app, including after the browser's local data is reset",
        "Existing tasks without a due date still load and behave as before"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-010",
      "title": "Due date display and overdue",
      "text": "The system shall show the due date next to each task that has one and visibly mark an open task as overdue when its due date is before today's date in the user's local time zone.",
      "type": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptanceCriteria": [
        "A task with a due date shows that date next to its text",
        "A task without a due date shows no date",
        "An open task with a due date before today (user's local date) is visibly marked overdue",
        "An open task with a due date of today or later is not marked overdue",
        "A done task is never marked overdue, even if its due date is past",
        "A task without a due date is never marked overdue",
        "Unticking a done task whose due date is past marks it overdue",
        "The list order defined in REQ-007 is unchanged by due dates"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "openQuestions": [],
  "assumptions": [],
  "outOfScope": [
    "User accounts, login and multi-user support",
    "Priorities and categories",
    "Browser-only storage as the sole persistence"
  ]
}

name: read_design

actors.name: User
actors.description: The single user of the task list, no login.

useCases.name: View task list
useCases.description: Open the app and see tasks, open first then done, oldest first in each group; due dates do not change the order. The Browser page shows each done task with a ticked checkbox and struck-through text, and each open task with an empty checkbox and plain text. A task with a due date shows the date next to its text. The page sends its local date as the today query parameter of GET /api/tasks and the server returns each task with an overdue flag (open, has a due date before today); the page marks tasks with overdue true. Done tasks and tasks without a due date are never overdue.

useCases.name: Add task
useCases.description: Enter a description (trimmed, 1-200 chars) and optionally a due date (date only, YYYY-MM-DD) to add a not-done task. An invalid date or description creates no task.

useCases.name: Mark task done or not done
useCases.description: Tick or untick a task. The Browser page sends PATCH /api/tasks/:id with done true or false, then re-renders that task from the returned Task: done shows a ticked checkbox and struck-through text, not done shows an empty checkbox and plain text, so the two states look different. The task moves to its place in the open or done group. Unticking a task with a past due date marks it overdue; the page reloads the list with its local date so the server's overdue flag is current.

useCases.name: Edit task
useCases.description: Change the text and the optional due date of a task with the same rules as adding. The due date can be set, changed or cleared. An invalid text or date is rejected and the stored values are kept; the done state is kept.

classes.name: Task
classes.description: Task data record. dueDate is a calendar date string YYYY-MM-DD without time, or null when the task has none; existing tasks without one load as null.

classes.name: TaskView
classes.description: A Task as returned by GET /api/tasks, with the overdue flag computed by the server for the date the page sent.

classes.name: TaskController
classes.description: HTTP routes: GET /, GET /api/tasks (optional today query parameter, YYYY-MM-DD, the page's local date; returns tasks with an overdue flag), POST /api/tasks, PATCH /api/tasks/:id, DELETE /api/tasks/:id. Serves the single page without login. PATCH returns the updated Task so the page can re-render it. Bodies may carry dueDate (YYYY-MM-DD or null to clear).

params.name: body
params.type: { text?: string; done?: boolean; dueDate?: string | null; }

classes.name: TaskService
classes.description: Validates text (trim, 1-200 chars) and optional due date (valid calendar date, no time), applies rules and orders the list by done state then creation time, independent of due dates. isOverdue is true only for an open task with a due date strictly before today (YYYY-MM-DD string comparison); list(today) adds that flag to each task, rejects an invalid today, and uses the server date when today is omitted.

classes.name: TaskStore
classes.description: SQLite persistence of tasks inside the service process, including the nullable due date column; rows without a due date load with null.

rows.note: Purely visual, rendered by the browser page, which has no classes; described in UC-001 and UC-003.
Non-functional; satisfied by the Browser page component and the http link.
Strike-through is rendered by the browser page, which has no classes; described in UC-001.

text:
The overdue rule is now on the server and saved. The browser still has no classes.

- **`TaskService.isOverdue(task, today)`:** it returns true only for an open task with a due date strictly before `today`, compared as YYYY-MM-DD strings. Done tasks and tasks without a due date are never overdue.
- **`TaskService.list(today?)`:** it adds the `overdue` flag to each task. It rejects an invalid `today` and falls back to the server date if `today` is missing.
- **`GET /api/tasks`:** `TaskController.list` takes the optional `today` query parameter and returns `TaskView[]`.
- **`TaskView`:** a new interface (DSN-009) that extends `Task` with `overdue: boolean`.
- **Sequence and use cases:** SEQ-001 has a new `isOverdue` step, and UC-001 and UC-003 describe how the page sends its local date and uses the flag.

All five REQ-010 overdue criteria (3 to 7) are now covered by methods.

- **Unticking:** PATCH still returns a plain `Task` with no overdue flag, since you only asked for the GET change. So after unticking, the page reloads the list with its local date to get the flag. If you want PATCH to return the flag too, say so.
- **Still uncovered:** two criteria are purely visual, rendered by the classless browser page. They are REQ-002 criterion 3 (the done state looks different) and REQ-007 criterion 1 (struck-through text for a done task). Both are described in the use cases.
